concepts.title: What Is a Civilisation?
concepts.definition: A civilisation is an advanced stage of human society marked by government and administration, urbanism with town planning and cities, and shared systems such as writing, trade and technology.
concepts.key_idea: A civilisation is more than villages: it is society grown complex, with cities, officials and records.

concepts.title: The Harappan Civilisation
concepts.definition: The most ancient civilisation of the Indian subcontinent is known as the Harappan, Indus or Indus-Sarasvati Civilisation; it flourished along the Indus and the Sarasvati's course over four thousand years ago.
concepts.key_idea: One civilisation, three names: Harappan from the first site, Indus and Indus-Sarasvati from its rivers.

concepts.title: Harappan Towns: Planning and Achievements
concepts.definition: Harappan cities show careful town planning with grid streets, covered drains, fortified areas like Dholavira's castle, standardized bricks and weights, seals and bead work, and trade reaching distant lands.
concepts.key_idea: Streets, drains and standard weights reveal a government that planned and a people that followed rules together.

concepts.title: Harappan Society: Decline and Legacy
concepts.definition: Harappan society was balanced rather than exploitative, with no glaring gulf between rich and poor; around 1900 BCE the cities declined, yet their farming, crafts, and town ways passed into later Indian life.
concepts.key_idea: What survives a civilisation's fall is its legacy: the Harappan ways quietly seeded the culture that followed.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why are the Harappan cities called well planned?

solution_template.explain: Streets cut across each other in grids and drains run covered beneath them.
Such order needs shared measurements and some authority, marks of an advanced society.

worked_examples.question_pattern: How do we know the Harappans traded far away?

solution_template.explain: Thousands of carved seals and standard weights mark goods and bargains.
Materials from distant lands found in Harappan cities show ships carried trade across the seas.
